Goal: safely restore strength, work capacity and body mass after 3-week illness break. Primary priorities: rebuild tolerance to training stress, re-establish technical patterns for main lifts, gradually increase volume and intensity, monitor fatigue and recovery, encourage adequate nutrition and sleep to regain weight. Avoid aggressive loading — favor conservative intensities with focus on movement quality and autoregulation.

General guidance for the block
- Frequency: 4 sessions/week (two upper, two lower) — enough stimulus without overstress.
- Structure: Each week slightly increases volume or intensity; include an easy day midweek progression and active recovery elements.
- Intensity approach: use percentages of pre-illness 1RMs as reference but reduce them early. Aim for Rate of Perceived Exertion (RPE) 6–8 on main work sets. If persistent fatigue or symptoms return, back off volume by ~20% or substitute lighter session.
- Warm-ups: 8–12 minutes general (bike/row/light jog) + joint mobility and movement prep for the session; perform progressively heavier technical warm sets before main lifts.
- Rest: 48–72 hours between similar stressors; monitor sleep, HR, and subjective fatigue daily.
- Nutrition: aim to regain weight gradually — target ~+300–500 kcal/day above current maintenance (protein 1.6–2.2 g/kg bodyweight; if 41yo male ~80–90 kg? adjust accordingly). Prioritize 3 meals + 1–2 snacks: high-quality carbs around training, adequate protein per meal (25–40 g). Rehydrate, include electrolytes if needed.
- Recovery: prioritize 7–9 hours sleep; consider low-intensity cardio, mobility, and sauna/contrast only if tolerated. Avoid hard conditioning until Week 3 and only light conditioning in Weeks 1–2.
- Monitoring: track session RPE, pre-session resting HR, sleep hours, appetite. If performance drops >10% or fatigue accumulates, deload or repeat lower-volume week.

Reference intensities (use pre-illness maxes as baseline)
- Bench 1RM = 100 kg; Squat 1RM = 140 kg; Deadlift 1RM = 170 kg.
- Week 1 work intensities will be ~50–65% for heavy patterns, Week 2 ~60–75%, Week 3 ~70–80% for single top sets; keep rep ranges conservative and avoid true 1RM attempts.

3-week Reconditioning Block — 4 sessions/week
Layout: 
- Day A: Upper Strength Emphasis (bench + upper accessory)
- Day B: Lower Strength Emphasis (squat + posterior chain)
- Day C: Upper Hypertrophy/Volume and Pull Emphasis
- Day D: Lower Hypertrophy/Deadlift Focus + Conditioning (light)

Week 1 — very conservative reintroduction (focus on movement and volume tolerance)
Session A (Upper Strength) — ~60–70 minutes
- Warm-up: 8–10 min bike + shoulder/thoracic mobility, band pull-aparts, scap protraction.
- Bench press: 4 sets x 6 reps @ ~55% (≈55 kg) — last set RPE ~7. Use 2–3 warm-up sets.
- Incline dumbbell press: 3 x 8–10 @ moderate weight RPE 7.
- Seated cable row (or chest-supported row): 3 x 10–12.
- Overhead press (standing or seated dumbbell): 3 x 8 (lighter).
- Face pulls: 3 x 15 (control).
- Core: Plank 3 x 30–45s.
Notes: Keep rest 90–150s on compound lifts, 60–90s on accessories.

Session B (Lower Strength) — ~65–75 minutes
- Warm-up: 8–10 min bike/row + hip mobility, bodyweight squats, glute bridges.
- Squat (high-bar or preferred): 4 x 5 @ ~60% (≈85 kg) — controlled tempo. 2–3 technical warm-up sets.
- Romanian deadlift: 3 x 8 @ moderate weight (focus on hinge).
- Bulgarian split squat: 3 x 8 each leg.
- Hamstring curl (machine) or glute-ham raise: 3 x 10–12.
- Calf raises: 3 x 12–15.
- Core: Dead bug 3 x 10/side.
Notes: Pay attention to breathing, bracing, and knee/hip comfort.

Session C (Upper Volume/Pull) — ~60 minutes
- Warm-up: 8–10 min row + scap/rotator cuff work.
- Pull-ups or assisted pull-ups: 4 x 6–8 (use band/assistance if needed).
- Dumbbell bench or flat DB press: 3 x 10–12 (moderate).
- Bent-over barbell row (or T-bar row): 4 x 8.
- Lateral raises: 3 x 12–15.
- Biceps curl superset with triceps pushdown: 3 x 10–12 each.
- Mobility/Thoracic extension: 5–8 min.
Notes: Keep session tempo steady; don't chase PRs.

Session D (Lower Volume + Deadlift) — ~60 minutes
- Warm-up: 8–10 min bike + dynamic hamstring/hip mobility.
- Trap-bar deadlift or conventional, technique focus: 3 x 5 @ ~60% (≈100 kg if deadlift 170; trap-bar percentage similar) — use trap-bar if lower back feels fatigued.
- Front squat or goblet squat: 3 x 8.
- Single-leg Romanian deadlift: 3 x 8/leg.
- Reverse lunges: 3 x 10 total.
- Light conditioning: 10–12 min easy bike or walk (zone 1–2).
- Core: Pallof press 3 x 10/side.
Notes: Keep lower-back volume moderate; prioritize form.

Week 2 — increase volume and intensity slightly; test tolerance
Progression principle: increase a set or add 1–2 reps, raise working intensities by ~5–10% relative to Week 1, maintain RPE 7–8 on last sets.

Session A (Upper Strength) 
- Bench press: 5 x 5 @ ~62% (≈62 kg). Last set RPE ~7.5.
- Close-grip bench or paused bench: 3 x 6 (pause 1s) @ moderate.
- Pendlay or chest-supported rows: 4 x 8.
- Overhead press: 3 x 6–8 (slightly heavier).
- Face pulls: 3 x 15–20.
- Core: Side plank 3 x 30s each.

Session B (Lower Strength)
- Squat: 5 x 5 @ ~65% (≈90–95 kg).
- Romanian deadlift: 4 x 6–8 (slightly heavier).
- Walking lunges: 3 x 12 steps.
- Nordic curl alternative or hamstring curl: 3 x 8–10.
- Calf raises: 4 x 12.

Session C (Upper Volume/Pull)
- Pull-ups: 4 x 6–8 (aim for slightly more volume or less assistance).
- Flat dumbbell bench: 4 x 8–10.
- Barbell row: 4 x 6–8 (slightly heavier).
- Lateral raises: 4 x 12.
- Biceps/triceps superset: 3 x 10–12.
- Mobility: scap/pec/shoulder work.

Session D (Lower Volume + Deadlift)
- Deadlift: 4 x 4 @ ~70% (≈120 kg). Focus on clean setup and bar speed; RPE ~7.5.
- Front squat or paused goblet: 3 x 6–8.
- Single-leg RDL or good morning variation: 3 x 8.
- Hip thrust: 3 x 8–10 (moderate).
- Optional light conditioning: 10–15 min walk or easy bike.

Week 3 — approach baseline intensities but remain conservative; allow a top heavy set but avoid 1RMs
Goal: restore confidence with heavier singles/double sets but still leave reps in reserve.

Session A (Upper Strength)
- Bench press: Work up to 3 working sets: 3 x 3 @ ~75% (≈75 kg). Option: one back-off set 5 reps @ 65%.
- Incline DB press: 3 x 6–8.
- Barbell row: 4 x 6.
- Overhead press: 3 x 5.
- Face pulls: 3 x 20.
- Core: Anti-rotation holds 3 x 8/side.

Session B (Lower Strength)
- Squat: 4 x 4 @ ~72% (≈100–105 kg). Consider one set of 2–3 reps at ~78% if fatigue is low.
- Romanian deadlift: 3 x 6.
- Bulgarian split squat: 3 x 8.
- Hamstring curl: 3 x 10.
- Calf raises: 4 x 12–15.

Session C (Upper Volume/Pull)
- Pull-ups/chin-ups: 5 x 5–8 (as many quality reps).
- Flat DB bench: 4 x 6–8 heavier.
- Seated cable row or chest-supported row: 4 x 8.
- Lateral raises: 4 x 12–15.
- Arm superset: 3 x 8–10.
- Mobility and thoracic work.

Session D (Lower Deadlift Focus)
- Deadlift: 3 x 3 @ ~80% (≈135 kg) — stop if technique or recovery suffers. Alternatively, do 2 x 2 @ ~85% only if feeling fresh.
- Front squat or pause squat: 3 x 5–6.
- Hip thrust: 3 x 6–8 heavier.
- Back extension or reverse hyper (if available): 3 x 10.
- Short conditioning: 10–15 min easy bike or sled push light.

Progression notes after Week 3
- Expect to be near baseline strengths but not necessarily at full 1RMs. After this block, assess weights: if energy and numbers look good, plan a 4–6 week strength phase progressing to heavier intensities, including possible testing of 1RMs only if fully recovered.
- Weight regain: keep caloric surplus and ensure protein intake. If persistent fatigue and continued weight loss, get medical follow-up.

Auto-regulation rules (must follow during block)
- If pre-session resting HR is >8–10 bpm above normal baseline or sleep <5–6 hours and feeling very lethargic, convert to an easier session: reduce intensity by ~20% and cut accessory volume by half.
- If a main lift feels heavy and technique degrades, stop increasing load and perform back-off set(s) with 5–10% less weight.

Why you should be cautious (brief)
- Recent illness + weight loss likely reduced glycogen, muscle mass, and systemic energy availability even if subjective energy feels normal — that reduces performance reserve.
- 3 weeks without heavy loading reduces tendon, ligament, and nervous system tolerance; sudden heavy loading increases injury risk.

- Avoid true 1RM attempts, heavy singles, max triples, or heavy deadlift volume for at least one more week.

- Keep accessory work at moderate loads and volume (RPE ~7).
- Keep running easy and modest volume as previously prescribed.

- Pre-session check: if resting HR >10 bpm above baseline, sleep <5 hours, or he reports unusual fatigue or flu symptoms, convert to an easy/recovery session.
- In-session: stop any set where technique degrades (rounded back, loss of control, bounce in bench), or when a set feels RPE ≥8. Reduce load 5–10% or cut volume.

- It supports gradual replenishment of glycogen and appetite, allowing you to increase calories and mass steadily.

Use a combination of performance markers, recovery metrics, health signs, and a short successful trial progression rather than a single trigger. Below are practical criteria and how to monitor them.

1) Short-term performance and training markers (primary)
- Progressive load tolerance for 7–14 days
  - He completes two consecutive weeks of planned progressive training with no unexpected setbacks (no large increases in soreness, no missed sessions due to fatigue/illness).
  - Each week shows stable or improving performance on main lifts (e.g., able to add the small planned increase in weight, reps, or sets without the session feeling disproportionately harder).
- RPE consistency
  - Working sets at prescribed loads land in the intended RPE window (e.g., RPE 6–8) and do not creep up significantly across sessions. If a weight that should be RPE 7 starts feeling RPE 9, regress.
- Ability to perform heavier singles/doubles with clean technique
  - He can execute heavier singles/doubles at ~80–85% of 1RM (or the intermediate progression you used) with flawless technique and normal bar speed across 2–3 sessions.

2) Objective recovery and physiological markers
- Resting heart rate (RHR) and heart rate variability (HRV)
  - RHR returns to his normal baseline (no persistent elevation of >6–8 bpm above baseline for several days).
  - If you use HRV, values return to typical pre-illness range (avoid a single-day read; look for trends).
- Sleep and energy
  - Consistent, quality sleep (7–9 hours/night) for at least 1–2 weeks and subjective energy is normal or improving throughout the day.
- Appetite and weight
  - Appetite has recovered and bodyweight is stable or moving back toward baseline (some regain of the 4 kg lost — expect part of this to come from glycogen and water initially).
- No ongoing illness symptoms
  - No fever, significant cough, chest tightness, shortness of breath on exertion, or prolonged unusual fatigue. If any return of systemic symptoms occurs, stop and reassess medically.
- Normal blood markers if previously abnormal or if clinically indicated
  - If he had notable weight loss, fatigue, or concerns, bloodwork (CBC, ferritin, TSH, vitamin D, basic metabolic panel) showing no significant abnormalities is reassuring before maximal loading. Not mandatory for everyone, but consider if recovery stalls.

3) Subjective readiness and daily check-ins
- Daily pre-session checklist (if all green, proceed):
  - Sleep ≥6–7 hours last night and restful.
  - Resting HR within normal range (or not >6–8 bpm above baseline).
  - Appetite normal or improving.
  - No excessive muscle soreness or joint pain that limits movement.
  - Mood/mental energy normal.
- If any item is red, treat that day as an easier session and re-test next day.

4) A planned ramp and test protocol (functional check)
Instead of an abrupt 1RM attempt, run a short test progression:
- Phase A: two weeks of progressive loading (example you already have) up to 70–80% with clean technique and no adverse signs.
- Phase B: perform controlled heavier work: 2–3 sessions where you test triples/doubles/singles at 85% and 90% (not maximal) — these should feel fast and technical with 1–2 reps in reserve.
- Only after successful Phase B (2–3 sessions across 7–10 days) with normal recovery do you consider 1RM testing or returning to heavy high-intensity block.

5) Practical numeric thresholds (examples)
- Bench: can hit planned 3 x 3 at ~75–80% with normal bar speed and RPE ≤8 for two sessions.
- Squat/deadlift: can perform doubles at ~80–85% with technical control and recovery intact for 2 sessions.
- Weight: regained at least 50–75% of the lost 4 kg (showing nutritional recovery) is a positive sign — not strictly required but helpful.
- Resting HR: ≤6 bpm above usual baseline on most mornings for a week.
- Sleep: average ≥7 hours/night for 5–7 days.

6) Red flags that require delaying full intensity
- New or recurrent systemic symptoms (fever, chest tightness, unexplained breathlessness).
- Progressive decline in performance, rising RPEs, or inability to complete planned sessions.
- Persistent elevation in resting HR (>8–10 bpm vs baseline) or poor HRV trend for >4–5 days.
- Ongoing marked weight loss or poor appetite despite nutritional efforts.
- Excessive DOMS that limits technique for multiple sessions.

7) How to proceed when criteria are met
- Begin with an intentional 1–2 week “heavy re-introduction” using heavy doubles/singles and not true 1RM attempts. Keep overall weekly volume moderately reduced compared with his pre-illness high-week (~10–20% lower) for the first week of heavy intensities.
- Closely monitor the recovery markers above for another 7–10 days after increasing intensity. If signs remain favorable, progressively return to prior programming including testing 1RMs if desired.

8) Practical checklist you (the coach) can use before allowing full-intensity week
- Has he completed 2 consecutive weeks of planned, progressively heavier training without setbacks? (Yes/No)
- Morning resting HR trend for past 7 days within normal range? (Yes/No)
- Sleep average past 7 days ≥7 hours/night? (Yes/No)
- Appetite and weight stable or improving? (Yes/No)
- No systemic symptoms? (Yes/No)
- Can he perform 85–90% singles/doubles with good technique across 2 sessions? (Yes/No)
If most answers are Yes, you can cautiously move to full intensity progression.

- Readiness is not a single feeling — it’s a pattern across training performance, recovery metrics (RHR/HRV/sleep), appetite/weight, and absence of symptoms.

Quick overview and priorities
- Client: 41 y/o male, intermediate lifter. Pre-illness 1RMs: Bench 100 kg, Squat 140 kg, Deadlift 170 kg. Recent three-week break with mild flu, 4 kg weight loss; currently reports normal energy.
- Primary aims: safely restore strength and tolerance to training stress, regain ~4 kg in a controlled way, reintroduce running up to 10 km/week, and obtain valid 1RMs in the back half of Week 3 to reset programming.
- Frequency: 4 gym sessions/week (Upper, Lower, Upper, Lower) + 2–3 easy runs/week in Week 1 ramping to test in Week 3. Strict autoregulation and daily monitoring applied.

Monitoring / gating rules (must be followed daily)

No new systemic symptoms (fever, chest tightness, undue breathlessness)? If any are red, convert to easier session (cut intensity ~20% and halve accessory volume) or rest.
- In-session: stop increasing load if technique degrades or set feels >RPE 8. Drop load 5–10% or cut volume.
- Post-session: monitor next 48 hrs for excessive fatigue / soreness / elevated RHR. If present, revert to lower-volume plan.

Nutrition (during the 3-week block)
- Goal: regain weight gradually; target +300–500 kcal/day above current maintenance. If current weight unknown, use 30–33 kcal/kg/day +300 kcal as starting point.
- Protein: 1.8–2.2 g/kg/day (distribute across 3–4 meals).
- Carbs: 4–6 g/kg/day (place carbs around training and runs).
- Fat: 20–30% of calories.
- Practical example (85 kg client): ~2850–3150 kcal/day; protein ~153–187 g/day; carbs ~340–510 g/day; fats to fill remaining calories (~80–110 g).
- If appetite low, use calorie-dense smoothies, full-fat dairy, nut butters, and creatine 3–5 g/day for strength and mass support.

Week-by-week plan (detailed)

Week 1 — conservative reintroduction with concrete working loads
Goal: re-establish movement patterns, rebuild tissue and CNS tolerance, keep loads conservative despite client saying he feels fine.

Gym frequency: 4 sessions (A Upper, B Lower, C Upper, D Lower/Deadlift)
Cardio: 2–3 easy runs total for ~6–8 km in the week (all easy conversational pace Zone 1–2). No intervals or hills.

Session A — Upper Strength (Day 1)
- Warm-up: 8–10 min bike, shoulder/thoracic mobility, band pull-aparts.
- Bench press: 4 x 6 @ 55 kg (working sets). Warm-ups: bar x8–10; 40 kg x5; 50 kg x3.
- Incline dumbbell press: 3 x 8–10 (moderate DBs, RPE ~7).
- Seated cable row / chest-supported row: 3 x 10–12.
- Overhead press (DB or bar): 3 x 8 (lighter).
- Face pulls: 3 x 15.
- Core: Plank 3 x 30–45 s.
- Rest: 90–150 s compound, 60–90 s accessories.

Session B — Lower Strength (Day 2)
- Warm-up: 8–10 min bike/row, hip mobility, bodyweight squats, glute bridges.
- Squat (preferred variation): 4 x 5 @ 85 kg (≈60% 1RM). Warm-ups: bar x8–10; 60 kg x5; 75 kg x3.
- Romanian deadlift: 3 x 8 (moderate load, hinge focus).
- Bulgarian split squat: 3 x 8 per leg (bodyweight to light DBs).
- Hamstring curl: 3 x 10–12.
- Calf raises: 3 x 12–15.
- Core: Dead bug 3 x10/side.

Session C — Upper Volume / Pull (Day 4)
- Warm-up: 8–10 min row, scap/rotator cuff activation.
- Pull-ups / assisted: 4 x 6–8 (use assistance if needed).
- Flat dumbbell bench: 3 x 10–12 (moderate).
- Bent-over barbell or T-bar row: 4 x 8.
- Lateral raises: 3 x 12–15.
- Biceps curl supersetted with triceps pushdown: 3 x 10–12 each.
- Mobility / thoracic extension: 5–8 min.

Session D — Lower + Deadlift (Day 5)
- Warm-up: 8–10 min bike, dynamic hamstring/hip mobility.
- Deadlift (conventional or trap-bar): 3 x 5 @ 100 kg (≈60% 1RM). Warm-ups: light hinge, 60 kg x5; 80 kg x3.
- Front squat or goblet squat: 3 x 8.
- Single-leg RDL: 3 x 8/leg.
- Reverse lunges: 3 x 10 total.
- Light conditioning: 10–12 min easy bike or walk.
- Core: Pallof press 3 x 10/side.

Week 1 Cardio (runs)
- Run 1 (after Day 2 if possible): 20 min easy run ≈2.5–3.5 km, Zone 1–2.
- Run 2 (active recovery day): 15–20 min easy run ≈2–3 km.
- Optional Run 3 (only if energy good): 20 min easy run ≈3–4 km.
- If RHR elevated, sleep poor, or fatigue reported, replace runs with easy walks.

Nutrition Week 1 focus
- Target +300–500 kcal/day above maintenance. Prioritize carbs around lifts/runs and 1.8–2.2 g/kg protein/day.
- Use smoothies if appetite low; creatine 3–5 g/day optional.

Week 2 — increase volume/intensity moderately; monitor closely
Goal: increase stress tolerance and approach moderate intensities. Keep RPEs around 7–8 for main work.

Session A — Upper Strength (Day 1)
- Bench press: 5 x 5 @ 62 kg (~62% 1RM). Warm-ups: bar x8–10; 40 kg x5; 55 kg x3.
- Close-grip or paused bench: 3 x 6 (moderate).
- Pendlay or chest-supported row: 4 x 8.
- Overhead press: 3 x 6–8.
- Face pulls: 3 x 15–20.
- Core: Side plank 3 x 30 s/side.

Session B — Lower Strength (Day 2)
- Squat: 5 x 5 @ 90 kg (~64% 1RM). Warm-ups: bar; 60 kg x5; 80 kg x3.
- Romanian deadlift: 4 x 6–8 (slightly heavier).
- Walking lunges: 3 x 12 steps.
- Hamstring curl / Nordic alternative: 3 x 8–10.
- Calf raises: 4 x 12.

Session C — Upper Volume / Pull (Day 4)
- Pull-ups: 4 x 6–8 (aim for less assistance / more volume).
- Flat DB bench: 4 x 8–10 (moderate).
- Barbell row: 4 x 6–8.
- Lateral raises: 4 x 12.
- Biceps/triceps superset: 3 x 10–12.
- Mobility work.

Session D — Lower + Deadlift (Day 5)
- Deadlift: 4 x 4 @ 120 kg (~70% 1RM). Warm-ups: light hinge sets then 95–100 kg x3.
- Front squat or paused goblet: 3 x 6–8.
- Single-leg RDL or good morning: 3 x 8.
- Hip thrust: 3 x 8–10.
- Optional light conditioning: 10–15 min walk / easy bike.

Week 2 Cardio
- Increase to 2–3 runs totaling ~6–8 km. Keep all runs easy; no intensity work. Prefer runs on non-heavy or lower-intensity days and at least 60–90 min after lifting if same day.

Week 2 Nutrition
- Maintain +300–500 kcal/day surplus; increase carbs to support heavier lifts. Monitor weight: expect some initial glycogen/water return.

Week 3 — heavier working sets and planned 1RM test in back half
Goal: approach pre-illness intensities for short top sets, then perform controlled 1RM testing in the back half of the week if prerequisites met.

Prerequisites to run the 1RM test (must be met)
- No setbacks in Weeks 1–2 (able to complete planned sessions).
- Resting HR near baseline for preceding 5–7 days (no persistent elevation >6–8 bpm).
- Sleep average ≥6–7 hrs/night for prior 5–7 nights.
- Appetite and bodyweight stable or trending up.
- No new systemic symptoms.
- Successful heavier singles/doubles earlier in Week 3 (e.g., 85% singles with good technique) — see sessions below.

Session A — Upper Strength (Day 1 of Week 3)
- Bench press: 3 x 3 @ 75 kg (~75% 1RM). Warm-ups: bar x8; 40 kg x5; 55 kg x3; 70 kg x1.
- Incline DB press: 3 x 6–8.
- Barbell row: 4 x 6.
- Overhead press: 3 x 5.
- Face pulls: 3 x 20.
- Core: Anti-rotation holds 3 x 8/side.

Session B — Lower Strength (Day 2 of Week 3)
- Squat: 4 x 4 @ 100–105 kg (~72–75% 1RM). Warm-ups: bar; 60 kg x5; 80 kg x3; 95 kg x1.
- Romanian deadlift: 3 x 6.
- Bulgarian split squat: 3 x 8.
- Hamstring curl: 3 x 10.
- Calf raises: 4 x 12–15.

Session C — Upper Volume / Pull (Day 4 of Week 3)
- Pull-ups: 5 x 5–8.
- Flat DB bench: 4 x 6–8 (heavier than Week 2).
- Seated cable row / chest-supported: 4 x 8.
- Lateral raises: 4 x 12–15.
- Arms superset: 3 x 8–10.
- Mobility and thoracic work.

Session D — Lower Deadlift Focus + 1RM test window (Day 5 or Day 6 of Week 3)
- Early in the week perform: Deadlift 3 x 3 @ 135 kg (~80% 1RM) to confirm heavy singles/doubles tolerance. If these feel good across two sessions, we clear the test in the back half of Week 3.
- Decide on 1RM test day placement:
  - Option A (single-day test, all three on one day): schedule test on Day 6 (allows 48+ hours after a heavy deadlift session). Order: Squat → Bench → Deadlift.
  - Option B (split test over two days for maximum freshness): Day 5 Squat + Bench; Day 6 Deadlift. Prefer this if any concern over fatigue.
- See detailed testing protocol below (exact warm-ups and attempt progressions) — do not test unless prerequisites met.

Week 3 Cardio
- Move running toward goal: 2–3 runs totaling ~8–10 km if recovery is good. All runs remain easy. Avoid running the day before 1RM testing or keep it very light (<20 min walk/jog).

Week 3 Nutrition
- Continue calorie surplus; consider +400–500 kcal on test day to ensure glycogen and energy. Pre-test meal 60–90 min prior with carbs + protein. Post-test meal 30–60 min after with carbs + protein for recovery.

1RM Testing protocol (back half Week 3) — safe controlled procedure
Prerequisite recap: Weeks 1–2 successful, RHR/sleep/appetite stable, heavier singles/doubles earlier in Week 3 tolerated.

Test order (single day): Squat → Bench → Deadlift
- Have spotters for squat and bench and coach feedback for all lifts.
- General warm-up 8–10 min cardio + mobility; then lift-specific warm-up progression.

Warm-up and attempt guide (use 3–4 min rest between heavy singles; 4–5+ min between different lifts)
- Squat warm-up (pre-illness 1RM 140 kg example)
  - Bar x 8–10
  - 55 kg (40%) x 5
  - 80 kg (55%) x 3
  - 100 kg (70%) x 2
  - 115–120 kg (82–85%) x 1
  - 125–130 kg (89–93%) x 1 (optional)
  - Test attempts: attempt 1 conservative predicted 1RM (e.g., 135 kg); if good, +2.5–5% next attempt (137.5–140 kg). Limit to 3 top attempts.
- Bench warm-up (pre-illness 1RM 100 kg example)
  - Bar x 8–10
  - 40–45 kg (40–45%) x 5
  - 55 kg (55%) x 3
  - 70–75 kg (70–75%) x 2
  - 80–85 kg (80–85%) x 1
  - Test attempts: attempt 1 conservative predicted 1RM (e.g., 95 kg); if good, +2.5–5% next attempt (97.5–100 kg), limit to 3 attempts.
- Deadlift warm-up (pre-illness 1RM 170 kg example)
  - Light hinge reps x 8–10
  - 60–70 kg x 5
  - 95–100 kg x 3
  - 120–130 kg x 2
  - 140–150 kg x 1
  - Test attempts: attempt 1 conservative predicted 1RM (e.g., 165 kg); if good, +2.5–5% next attempt (170–172.5 kg), limit to 3 attempts.

Attempt progression rules and safety
- Attempt 1: conservative predicted 1RM (based on Week 3 heavy work).
- Attempt 2: add 2.5–5% only if Attempt 1 felt fast, technical, and recovery is good.
- Attempt 3: add another 2.5% only if Attempt 2 felt easy and speed remained high.
- Stop if technique fails, bar speed markedly drops, RPE > 9, or client reports unusual pain/dizziness.
- If a lift fails, take at least 3–5 min, consider a 5–10% reduction and one safe retest rather than repeatedly trying the same heavy weight.

Post-test recovery (first 72 hrs)
- Immediate: light cooldown, rehydrate, hearty carb+protein meal. Gentle mobility.
- Next 48–72 hours: reduce volume 30–40% and intensity to ~60–70% on accessory work; avoid hard conditioning. Monitor RHR, sleep, soreness.
- If recovery poor, extend the reduced load period.

How to reset the programme after test
- Use tested 1RMs as the new baselines for percentage-based programming, but be conservative:
  - First 1–2 weeks post-test: use 60–75% of tested 1RMs with moderate volume to build tolerance (keep weekly volume ~10–20% lower than the highest pre-illness load).
  - Progress intensity and volume gradually over the next 4–6 weeks rather than immediately returning to heavy max-effort programming.
- If any tested 1RM is below pre-illness, accept it as current and progress from it; do not force a quick return to previous maxes.

Contingency: if client insists on jumping harder now (middle-ground)
- If he truly feels great and you agree to accelerate, use a middle-ground Week 1 alternative: work at ~70–75% of 1RMs for main lifts rather than full pre-illness loads. Example working weights:
  - Bench 70% = 70 kg (e.g., 4 x 4–5), Squat 70% = 98 kg (round to 100 kg; 4 x 3–4), Deadlift 70% = 119–120 kg (3 x 3). Strict autoregulation applies; revert immediately if any red flags.
- I still advise following the planned testing prerequisites before any true 1RM attempts.

Summary schedule (compact)
- Week 1: conservative working weights — Bench 4x6 @ 55 kg; Squat 4x5 @ 85 kg; Deadlift 3x5 @ 100 kg. Runs 2–3 easy totalling ~6–8 km. Nutrition +300–500 kcal surplus; protein 1.8–2.2 g/kg.
- Week 2: increase to Bench 5x5 @ 62 kg; Squat 5x5 @ 90 kg; Deadlift 4x4 @ 120 kg. Runs 2–3 easy; nutrition maintained.
- Week 3: higher intensity short sets Bench 3x3 @ 75 kg; Squat 4x4 @ 100–105 kg; Deadlift 3x3 @ 135 kg early in week; controlled 1RM test on Day 5/6 if prerequisites met. Post-test recovery 48–72 hrs reduced volume/intensity. Use tested 1RMs to reset programming.

If you want:
- I can print this as a one-page daily plan (with exact days for lifts and runs based on his preferred weekly schedule).
- I can calculate the post-test Week 4 template using the new tested 1RMs once you give me the measured results.
- I can produce a printable 1RM testing worksheet with exact warm-up sets and checkboxes for prerequisites and gating rules.

Proceed options for you now
- Confirm which day you’ll schedule the 1RM test (single-day or split) and I’ll provide a printable step-by-step test sheet tailored to that choice.
- Or confirm you want the one-page daily schedule for Week 1–3 laid out as “Day 1/Day 2…” with times and warm-up bullet points.

Below is the full 3-week reconditioning programme, updated to include: the concrete Week 1 working loads you requested earlier, the conservative ramp-up through Week 2 and Week 3, the added running plan, the nutrition targets for regaining weight, the safety/autoregulation rules you and the client agreed on, the option to accelerate to a middle-ground if he felt good (included as contingency), and a controlled 1RM test in the back half of Week 3 with prerequisites, warm-ups, attempt progressions, and post-test recovery/next steps.

Quick overview and priorities
- Client: 41 y/o male, intermediate lifter. Pre-illness 1RMs: Bench 100 kg, Squat 140 kg, Deadlift 170 kg. Recent three-week break with mild flu, 4 kg weight loss; currently reports normal energy.
- Primary aims: safely restore strength and tolerance to training stress, regain ~4 kg in a controlled way, reintroduce running up to 10 km/week, and obtain valid 1RMs in the back half of Week 3 to reset programming.
- Frequency: 4 gym sessions/week (Upper, Lower, Upper, Lower) + 2–3 easy runs/week in Week 1 ramping to test in Week 3. Strict autoregulation and daily monitoring applied.

Monitoring / gating rules (must be followed daily)
- Daily pre-session checklist: Sleep last night ≥6–7 hrs? Resting HR ≤ ~6–8 bpm above his baseline? Appetite normal or improving? No new systemic symptoms (fever, chest tightness, undue breathlessness)? If any are red, convert to easier session (cut intensity ~20% and halve accessory volume) or rest.
- In-session: stop increasing load if technique degrades or set feels >RPE 8. Drop load 5–10% or cut volume.
- Post-session: monitor next 48 hrs for excessive fatigue / soreness / elevated RHR. If present, revert to lower-volume plan.

Nutrition (during the 3-week block)
- Goal: regain weight gradually; target +300–500 kcal/day above current maintenance. If current weight unknown, use 30–33 kcal/kg/day +300 kcal as starting point.
- Protein: 1.8–2.2 g/kg/day (distribute across 3–4 meals).
- Carbs: 4–6 g/kg/day (place carbs around training and runs).
- Fat: 20–30% of calories.
- Practical example (85 kg client): ~2850–3150 kcal/day; protein ~153–187 g/day; carbs ~340–510 g/day; fats to fill remaining calories (~80–110 g).
- If appetite low, use calorie-dense smoothies, full-fat dairy, nut butters, and creatine 3–5 g/day for strength and mass support.

Week-by-week plan (detailed)

Week 1 — conservative reintroduction with concrete working loads
Goal: re-establish movement patterns, rebuild tissue and CNS tolerance, keep loads conservative despite client saying he feels fine.

Gym frequency: 4 sessions (A Upper, B Lower, C Upper, D Lower/Deadlift)
Cardio: 2–3 easy runs total for ~6–8 km in the week (all easy conversational pace Zone 1–2). No intervals or hills.

Session A — Upper Strength (Day 1)
- Warm-up: 8–10 min bike, shoulder/thoracic mobility, band pull-aparts.
- Bench press: 4 x 6 @ 55 kg (working sets). Warm-ups: bar x8–10; 40 kg x5; 50 kg x3.
- Incline dumbbell press: 3 x 8–10 (moderate DBs, RPE ~7).
- Seated cable row / chest-supported row: 3 x 10–12.
- Overhead press (DB or bar): 3 x 8 (lighter).
- Face pulls: 3 x 15.
- Core: Plank 3 x 30–45 s.
- Rest: 90–150 s compound, 60–90 s accessories.

Session B — Lower Strength (Day 2)
- Warm-up: 8–10 min bike/row, hip mobility, bodyweight squats, glute bridges.
- Squat (preferred variation): 4 x 5 @ 85 kg (≈60% 1RM). Warm-ups: bar x8–10; 60 kg x5; 75 kg x3.
- Romanian deadlift: 3 x 8 (moderate load, hinge focus).
- Bulgarian split squat: 3 x 8 per leg (bodyweight to light DBs).
- Hamstring curl: 3 x 10–12.
- Calf raises: 3 x 12–15.
- Core: Dead bug 3 x10/side.

Session C — Upper Volume / Pull (Day 4)
- Warm-up: 8–10 min row, scap/rotator cuff activation.
- Pull-ups / assisted: 4 x 6–8 (use assistance if needed).
- Flat dumbbell bench: 3 x 10–12 (moderate).
- Bent-over barbell or T-bar row: 4 x 8.
- Lateral raises: 3 x 12–15.
- Biceps curl supersetted with triceps pushdown: 3 x 10–12 each.
- Mobility / thoracic extension: 5–8 min.

Session D — Lower + Deadlift (Day 5)
- Warm-up: 8–10 min bike, dynamic hamstring/hip mobility.
- Deadlift (conventional or trap-bar): 3 x 5 @ 100 kg (≈60% 1RM). Warm-ups: light hinge, 60 kg x5; 80 kg x3.
- Front squat or goblet squat: 3 x 8.
- Single-leg RDL: 3 x 8/leg.
- Reverse lunges: 3 x 10 total.
- Light conditioning: 10–12 min easy bike or walk.
- Core: Pallof press 3 x 10/side.

Week 1 Cardio (runs)
- Run 1 (after Day 2 if possible): 20 min easy run ≈2.5–3.5 km, Zone 1–2.
- Run 2 (active recovery day): 15–20 min easy run ≈2–3 km.
- Optional Run 3 (only if energy good): 20 min easy run ≈3–4 km.
- If RHR elevated, sleep poor, or fatigue reported, replace runs with easy walks.

Nutrition Week 1 focus
- Target +300–500 kcal/day above maintenance. Prioritize carbs around lifts/runs and 1.8–2.2 g/kg protein/day.
- Use smoothies if appetite low; creatine 3–5 g/day optional.

Week 2 — increase volume/intensity moderately; monitor closely
Goal: increase stress tolerance and approach moderate intensities. Keep RPEs around 7–8 for main work.

Session A — Upper Strength (Day 1)
- Bench press: 5 x 5 @ 62 kg (~62% 1RM). Warm-ups: bar x8–10; 40 kg x5; 55 kg x3.
- Close-grip or paused bench: 3 x 6 (moderate).
- Pendlay or chest-supported row: 4 x 8.
- Overhead press: 3 x 6–8.
- Face pulls: 3 x 15–20.
- Core: Side plank 3 x 30 s/side.

Session B — Lower Strength (Day 2)
- Squat: 5 x 5 @ 90 kg (~64% 1RM). Warm-ups: bar; 60 kg x5; 80 kg x3.
- Romanian deadlift: 4 x 6–8 (slightly heavier).
- Walking lunges: 3 x 12 steps.
- Hamstring curl / Nordic alternative: 3 x 8–10.
- Calf raises: 4 x 12.

Session C — Upper Volume / Pull (Day 4)
- Pull-ups: 4 x 6–8 (aim for less assistance / more volume).
- Flat DB bench: 4 x 8–10 (moderate).
- Barbell row: 4 x 6–8.
- Lateral raises: 4 x 12.
- Biceps/triceps superset: 3 x 10–12.
- Mobility work.

Session D — Lower + Deadlift (Day 5)
- Deadlift: 4 x 4 @ 120 kg (~70% 1RM). Warm-ups: light hinge sets then 95–100 kg x3.
- Front squat or paused goblet: 3 x 6–8.
- Single-leg RDL or good morning: 3 x 8.
- Hip thrust: 3 x 8–10.
- Optional light conditioning: 10–15 min walk / easy bike.

Week 2 Cardio
- Increase to 2–3 runs totaling ~6–8 km. Keep all runs easy; no intensity work. Prefer runs on non-heavy or lower-intensity days and at least 60–90 min after lifting if same day.

Week 2 Nutrition
- Maintain +300–500 kcal/day surplus; increase carbs to support heavier lifts. Monitor weight: expect some initial glycogen/water return.

Week 3 — heavier working sets and planned 1RM test in back half
Goal: approach pre-illness intensities for short top sets, then perform controlled 1RM testing in the back half of the week if prerequisites met.

Prerequisites to run the 1RM test (must be met)
- No setbacks in Weeks 1–2 (able to complete planned sessions).
- Resting HR near baseline for preceding 5–7 days (no persistent elevation >6–8 bpm).
- Sleep average ≥6–7 hrs/night for prior 5–7 nights.
- Appetite and bodyweight stable or trending up.
- No new systemic symptoms.
- Successful heavier singles/doubles earlier in Week 3 (e.g., 85% singles with good technique) — see sessions below.

Session A — Upper Strength (Day 1 of Week 3)
- Bench press: 3 x 3 @ 75 kg (~75% 1RM). Warm-ups: bar x8; 40 kg x5; 55 kg x3; 70 kg x1.
- Incline DB press: 3 x 6–8.
- Barbell row: 4 x 6.
- Overhead press: 3 x 5.
- Face pulls: 3 x 20.
- Core: Anti-rotation holds 3 x 8/side.

Session B — Lower Strength (Day 2 of Week 3)
- Squat: 4 x 4 @ 100–105 kg (~72–75% 1RM). Warm-ups: bar; 60 kg x5; 80 kg x3; 95 kg x1.
- Romanian deadlift: 3 x 6.
- Bulgarian split squat: 3 x 8.
- Hamstring curl: 3 x 10.
- Calf raises: 4 x 12–15.

Session C — Upper Volume / Pull (Day 4 of Week 3)
- Pull-ups: 5 x 5–8.
- Flat DB bench: 4 x 6–8 (heavier than Week 2).
- Seated cable row / chest-supported: 4 x 8.
- Lateral raises: 4 x 12–15.
- Arms superset: 3 x 8–10.
- Mobility and thoracic work.

Session D — Lower Deadlift Focus + 1RM test window (Day 5 or Day 6 of Week 3)
- Early in the week perform: Deadlift 3 x 3 @ 135 kg (~80% 1RM) to confirm heavy singles/doubles tolerance. If these feel good across two sessions, we clear the test in the back half of Week 3.
- Decide on 1RM test day placement:
  - Option A (single-day test, all three on one day): schedule test on Day 6 (allows 48+ hours after a heavy deadlift session). Order: Squat → Bench → Deadlift.
  - Option B (split test over two days for maximum freshness): Day 5 Squat + Bench; Day 6 Deadlift. Prefer this if any concern over fatigue.
- See detailed testing protocol below (exact warm-ups and attempt progressions) — do not test unless prerequisites met.

Week 3 Cardio
- Move running toward goal: 2–3 runs totaling ~8–10 km if recovery is good. All runs remain easy. Avoid running the day before 1RM testing or keep it very light (<20 min walk/jog).

Week 3 Nutrition
- Continue calorie surplus; consider +400–500 kcal on test day to ensure glycogen and energy. Pre-test meal 60–90 min prior with carbs + protein. Post-test meal 30–60 min after with carbs + protein for recovery.

1RM Testing protocol (back half Week 3) — safe controlled procedure
Prerequisite recap: Weeks 1–2 successful, RHR/sleep/appetite stable, heavier singles/doubles earlier in Week 3 tolerated.

Test order (single day): Squat → Bench → Deadlift
- Have spotters for squat and bench and coach feedback for all lifts.
- General warm-up 8–10 min cardio + mobility; then lift-specific warm-up progression.

Warm-up and attempt guide (use 3–4 min rest between heavy singles; 4–5+ min between different lifts)
- Squat warm-up (pre-illness 1RM 140 kg example)
  - Bar x 8–10
  - 55 kg (40%) x 5
  - 80 kg (55%) x 3
  - 100 kg (70%) x 2
  - 115–120 kg (82–85%) x 1
  - 125–130 kg (89–93%) x 1 (optional)
  - Test attempts: attempt 1 conservative predicted 1RM (e.g., 135 kg); if good, +2.5–5% next attempt (137.5–140 kg). Limit to 3 top attempts.
- Bench warm-up (pre-illness 1RM 100 kg example)
  - Bar x 8–10
  - 40–45 kg (40–45%) x 5
  - 55 kg (55%) x 3
  - 70–75 kg (70–75%) x 2
  - 80–85 kg (80–85%) x 1
  - Test attempts: attempt 1 conservative predicted 1RM (e.g., 95 kg); if good, +2.5–5% next attempt (97.5–100 kg), limit to 3 attempts.
- Deadlift warm-up (pre-illness 1RM 170 kg example)
  - Light hinge reps x 8–10
  - 60–70 kg x 5
  - 95–100 kg x 3
  - 120–130 kg x 2
  - 140–150 kg x 1
  - Test attempts: attempt 1 conservative predicted 1RM (e.g., 165 kg); if good, +2.5–5% next attempt (170–172.5 kg), limit to 3 attempts.

Attempt progression rules and safety
- Attempt 1: conservative predicted 1RM (based on Week 3 heavy work).
- Attempt 2: add 2.5–5% only if Attempt 1 felt fast, technical, and recovery is good.
- Attempt 3: add another 2.5% only if Attempt 2 felt easy and speed remained high.
- Stop if technique fails, bar speed markedly drops, RPE > 9, or client reports unusual pain/dizziness.
- If a lift fails, take at least 3–5 min, consider a 5–10% reduction and one safe retest rather than repeatedly trying the same heavy weight.

Post-test recovery (first 72 hrs)
- Immediate: light cooldown, rehydrate, hearty carb+protein meal. Gentle mobility.
- Next 48–72 hours: reduce volume 30–40% and intensity to ~60–70% on accessory work; avoid hard conditioning. Monitor RHR, sleep, soreness.
- If recovery poor, extend the reduced load period.

How to reset the programme after test
- Use tested 1RMs as the new baselines for percentage-based programming, but be conservative:
  - First 1–2 weeks post-test: use 60–75% of tested 1RMs with moderate volume to build tolerance (keep weekly volume ~10–20% lower than the highest pre-illness load).
  - Progress intensity and volume gradually over the next 4–6 weeks rather than immediately returning to heavy max-effort programming.
- If any tested 1RM is below pre-illness, accept it as current and progress from it; do not force a quick return to previous maxes.

Contingency: if client insists on jumping harder now (middle-ground)
- If he truly feels great and you agree to accelerate, use a middle-ground Week 1 alternative: work at ~70–75% of 1RMs for main lifts rather than full pre-illness loads. Example working weights:
  - Bench 70% = 70 kg (e.g., 4 x 4–5), Squat 70% = 98 kg (round to 100 kg; 4 x 3–4), Deadlift 70% = 119–120 kg (3 x 3). Strict autoregulation applies; revert immediately if any red flags.
- I still advise following the planned testing prerequisites before any true 1RM attempts.

Summary schedule (compact)
- Week 1: conservative working weights — Bench 4x6 @ 55 kg; Squat 4x5 @ 85 kg; Deadlift 3x5 @ 100 kg. Runs 2–3 easy totalling ~6–8 km. Nutrition +300–500 kcal surplus; protein 1.8–2.2 g/kg.
- Week 2: increase to Bench 5x5 @ 62 kg; Squat 5x5 @ 90 kg; Deadlift 4x4 @ 120 kg. Runs 2–3 easy; nutrition maintained.
- Week 3: higher intensity short sets Bench 3x3 @ 75 kg; Squat 4x4 @ 100–105 kg; Deadlift 3x3 @ 135 kg early in week; controlled 1RM test on Day 5/6 if prerequisites met. Post-test recovery 48–72 hrs reduced volume/intensity. Use tested 1RMs to reset programming.

If you want:
- I can print this as a one-page daily plan (with exact days for lifts and runs based on his preferred weekly schedule).
- I can calculate the post-test Week 4 template using the new tested 1RMs once you give me the measured results.
- I can produce a printable 1RM testing worksheet with exact warm-up sets and checkboxes for prerequisites and gating rules.

Proceed options for you now
- Confirm which day you’ll schedule the 1RM test (single-day or split) and I’ll provide a printable step-by-step test sheet tailored to that choice.
- Or confirm you want the one-page daily schedule for Week 1–3 laid out as “Day 1/Day 2…” with times and warm-up bullet points.
